facts.statement: Globidens is an extinct genus of predatory marine lizard belonging to the family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: Globidens belongs to the family Mosasauridae, which consists of several genera of predatory marine lizards of various sizes that were prevalent during the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Globidens is famous for its highly rounded, globe-like teeth, which inspired its name.
facts.quote: Among mosasaurs, Globidens is probably most well known for the highly rounded, globe-like teeth that give it its name.

facts.statement: The first species of Globidens, G. alabamaensis, was described by Charles W. Gilmore in 1912.
facts.quote: Globidens alabamaensis was the first species of Globidens described, in a publication by Charles W. Gilmore (1912).

facts.statement: Fossils of Globidens have been found in Angola, Brazil, Colombia, Morocco, Syria, and the United States.
facts.quote: Specimens of Globidens have been discovered in Angola, Brazil, Colombia, Morocco, Syria and the United States.

facts.statement: Globidens was a medium-sized mosasaur that measured approximately 5 to 6 meters in length.
facts.quote: Globidens was a relatively medium-sized mosasaur, measuring about 5 - 6 m long.

facts.statement: Globidens possessed semispherical teeth with rounded points specifically adapted for crushing tough, armored prey like turtles, ammonites, nautili, and bivalves.
facts.quote: Globidens had semispherical teeth with rounded points suited for crushing tough, armored prey, including turtles, ammonites, nautili, and bivalves.

facts.statement: Globidens had a robust skull and a strong bite capable of penetrating the armor of shelled prey.
facts.quote: Like its larger relative, Mosasaurus, Globidens had a robustly built skull with tightly-articulating jaws and a strong bite that played a large role in the animal's ability to penetrate the armor of its shelled prey.

facts.statement: The genus Globidens was first described in 1912 by Charles W. Gilmore.
facts.quote: Globidens was first described in 1912 by Charles W. Gilmore.

facts.statement: Gilmore originally identified Globidens based on an incomplete specimen consisting of a partial skull, teeth, a cervical vertebra, and fragments.
facts.quote: Using an incomplete specimen made of only of a partial skull with several teeth, a single cervical vertebra, and numerous fragments, Gilmore identified Globidens as a new genus and named his type specimen Globidens alabamaensis.

facts.statement: The precise original location of the type specimen used by Gilmore is not precisely known.
facts.quote: However, it may be noted that the original location from which the specimen was taken is not precisely known, as Gilmore was examining a specimen that had been collected earlier.

facts.statement: Recovery of a complete mandible and partial skull revealed large jaw muscle attachment points indicative of a diet of hard-shelled prey.
facts.quote: A complete mandible and partial skull was recovered, showing large jaw adductor musculature attachment points indicative of hard shelled prey.

facts.statement: Globidens is believed to have been a durophagous predator that ate hard-shelled mollusks like bivalves and ammonites.
facts.quote: It is believed that Globidens was a durophagous predator, eating hard-shelled mollusks such as bivalves and ammonites.

facts.statement: Stomach contents from a specimen found in South Dakota contained crushed shells of inoceramid clams.
facts.quote: Stomach contents of a specimen found in South Dakota support prior assumptions, showing the crushed shells of inoceramid clams.

facts.statement: Globidens is classified within the subfamily Mosasaurinae and the tribe Globidensini.
facts.quote: Globidens resides within the subfamily Mosasaurinae, which includes several mosasaur lineages, and within that, the Tribe Globidensini, which also includes the genus Carinodens.

facts.statement: Carinodens is regarded as a sister taxon to Globidens.
facts.quote: Carinodens is thus regarded as a sister taxon of Globidens.

facts.statement: The specific phylogenetic placement of Globidens is somewhat unclear and varies between different studies.
facts.quote: Placement of Globidens and, to an extent, Mosasauridae in a phylogenetic tree is somewhat unclear and specific placement of genera varies between many morphological and molecular tests.

facts.statement: Globidens lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America, Morocco, Angola, and Indonesia.
facts.quote: Globidens ("dientes de globo") es un género de saurópsidos mosasáuridos, que vivieron en el Cretácico superior, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica, Marruecos, Angola e Indonesia.

facts.statement: Globidens reached a length of 6 meters.
facts.quote: Globidens medía 6 m de longitud

facts.statement: Globidens possessed nearly 40 round teeth that were similar in size to golf balls.
facts.quote: Muchos de los casi 40 dientes que tenía eran redondos como pelotas de golf y de un tamaño similar

facts.statement: The teeth were embedded in the jaw so that only the tops were visible.
facts.quote: Lejos de sobresalir, se encontraban incrustados en la mandíbula, de modo que solo se vea la parte superior

facts.statement: This dentition was ideal for crushing the thick shells of mollusks like clams or hard-bodied crabs.
facts.quote: Una dentadura así resultaba ideal para aplastar las gruesas conchas de moluscos como las almejas o los cangrejos de cuerpo duro

facts.statement: The long, peg-shaped front teeth likely allowed Globidens to extract mollusks from the sea floor or pull them from rocks.
facts.quote: Los dientes frontales eran largos y con forma de clavija, y Globidens pudo usarlos para extraer los moluscos del fondo marino o arrancarlos de las rocas

facts.statement: The genus Globidens was named by Gilmore in 1912.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Globidens (genus), Gilmore 1912

facts.statement: Globidens belongs to the subfamily Globidensini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Globidensini

facts.statement: Globidens is classified within the family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Mosasauridae

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Globidens is Globidens alabamensis.
facts.quote: Type species: Globidens alabamensis

facts.statement: Globidens lived from the Coniacian to the Maastrichtian, between 89.8 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Maastrichtian (89.8 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 32 recorded fossil occurrences of Globidens.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 32
